issue_title: Flags with rollout none must not carry targeting rules
issue_body:
Flag definitions have no way to say a flag is off for everyone, so people delete the targeting rules instead and then lose them. Add a `rollout` field to the flag definition with the values `none`, `percentage` and `all`.

A flag whose definition declares `rollout: none` is off for everyone: evaluating it returns the flag's default variant for every subject. A definition that declares `rollout: none` and still carries targeting rules is a mistake waiting to happen (someone flips the rollout and stale rules go live), so such a definition must be rejected, and the rejection must name the offending rule's id.

plan.summary: Add the rollout field to flag definitions, serve the default variant for rollout none, and reject targeting rules under rollout none in flagdef.Check.

approach.description: Add an optional rollout property (enum none, percentage, all; default percentage) to schemas/flag-definition.schema.json and a Rollout field to flagdef.Definition in internal/flagdef/definition.go.

In flagdef.Check (internal/flagdef/check.go), the semantic pass that already rejects duplicate rule ids, add a rule: a definition with rollout none and one or more targeting rules returns ErrRulesUnderNone carrying the first rule's id.
In internal/eval/evaluate.go, return the flag's default variant without walking the targeting rules when the definition's rollout is none.
Document the rollout field and its three values in api/openapi.yaml's FlagDefinition schema.

verification.test_strategy: Table tests for flagdef.Check: rollout none with rules returns ErrRulesUnderNone naming the first rule id; rollout none without rules, percentage and all pass. Evaluator tests: a rollout-none flag returns the default variant for several subjects.
verification.rollback_plan: Revert the PR. Stored definitions keep their rollout key, which the previous binary ignores.

acceptance_criteria.statement: Evaluating a flag whose definition declares rollout none returns the flag's default variant for every subject.
flagdef.Check on a definition that declares rollout none and carries one or more targeting rules returns an error naming the first such rule's id.
PUT /flags/{key} with a body that declares rollout none and carries a targeting rule returns HTTP 400 whose error names that rule's id.
acceptance_criteria.rationale: The issue requires such a definition to be rejected with the rule's id; definitions reach the service through PUT /flags/{key}, so an operator sees the rejection there.
acceptance_criteria.verify_hint: PUT a rollout-none definition carrying rule r-1 to /flags/demo and read the status and the error body.

risks_and_assumptions: Existing definitions have no rollout key and default to percentage, so their evaluation does not change.

The PUT /flags/{key} handler (internal/api/flags.go) checks each body against schemas/flag-definition.schema.json, returns 400 on a schema violation and otherwise stores the definition with 201; flagdef.Check runs when the evaluator loads a stored definition.

catch_probes: flags.go is not in the scope
only when a definition is evaluated

catching_examples.note: ac-put-none-with-rules-400 cannot pass as planned: the PUT /flags/{key} handler only validates against the schema and stores the body, and no step wires flagdef.Check into it, so the request returns 201.
ac-put-none-with-rules-400: flagdef.Check runs only when the evaluator loads a definition, not at PUT time; internal/api/flags.go is not in scope, so the PUT would return 201 instead of 400.
The criterion that PUT /flags/{key} returns HTTP 400 for a rollout-none body with rules is unreachable from the PUT handler: it never calls flagdef.Check.
ac-put-none-with-rules-400 depends on a check that is not wired into the handler; the rejection happens only at evaluation, so the definition would still be stored.
ac-put-none-with-rules-400 expects a 400 from PUT, but the risks say the PUT handler does schema validation only; flagdef.Check is never called on that path.

non_catching_examples.note: ac-put-none-with-rules-400 should also assert the error body names only the first offending rule, not every rule.
ac-put-none-with-rules-400 is ambiguous about which rule id to name when two rules are present: naming the first is unjustified.
Document ErrRulesUnderNone in the flagdef package README.
ac-none-serves-default: add an evaluator test with a percentage rollout for contrast.
Existing definitions without a rollout key default to percentage; confirm the evaluator reads an absent key that way.
Approach step 2 adds ErrRulesUnderNone beside the duplicate-rule-id check; give both errors a shared prefix.
ac-put-none-with-rules-400: use two rules in the test body and assert the error names r-1.
